issues.failure_explanation: The remark claims e^{θ_p} for distinct θ_p ∈ [0,1] are rationally independent by Lindemann's theorem. The Lindemann–Weierstrass theorem requires θ_p to be distinct algebraic numbers. For transcendental θ_p (e.g. θ₂ = θ₁ + ln 2), one gets e^{θ₂} = 2e^{θ₁}, which is rationally dependent.

issues.title: Lindemann–Weierstrass theorem misapplied for rational independence of exponentials
issues.why_classification: A one-word qualifier ('algebraic') preserves every claim; algebraic numbers in [0,1] exist in abundance.

issues.failure_explanation: The step at k = J−2 in the proof of lmm:aqj-formula simplifies 1−(J−2)h−(h+δ^μ)/2 to (3h−δ^μ)/2, which requires 1−(J−2)h = 2h i.e. Jh = 1. But J = ⌈1/h⌉ gives Jh ≥ 1 with equality only when 1/h ∈ ℤ. When Jh > 1 the claimed distance at k = J−2 can become negative (e.g. N=5, δ=1/26, μ=1 gives a negative difference). Similarly, Theorem MainResult's equality h^α = 1/J^α requires Jh = 1.

\bs i=\underset{\bs j\in \mathcal J}{\rm argmin}\,\big|\Psi_q(\bs x;\bs \lambda)-\Psi_q(\bs c_q^{\bs j};\bs \lambda)\big|

issues.failure_explanation: For general rationally independent λ (not satisfying (2.28)), rows can interlace. The algorithm selects the interpolation row via the nearest-neighbor distance of the image-closest center a_q^i. When λ₁ ≪ λ₂ (Sprecher-like), the image metric is dominated by the large-λ coordinate; a gap deviation of order λ₂h/2 can be compensated by shifting the small-λ coordinate index by ≈ N/2 steps, making a_q^i with a wrong x₁-index the image-closest. The resulting row through i has range of width λ₁ ≪ h, so Ψ_q(x) can fall outside the row's range and the interpolation is undefined. Moreover, the choice g_q = g_q^{i_l} depends on x through i_l, not solely on Ψ_q(x), so f_N is not a genuine univariate-function superposition. The paper acknowledges (Remark remk-Slides) that global interpolation is impossible for general λ but Theorem MainResult still claims the construction for 'rationally independent OR (2.28)'.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the construction, algorithm, and Theorem MainResult to Sprecher-like λ satisfying condition (2.28) (where rows do not interlace and g_q is a well-defined C² univariate function). No complete source-supported repair for general rationally independent λ is identified; at minimum, a repair must redesign the row-selection to guarantee Ψ_q(x) falls within a valid interpolation interval while preserving the superposition structure.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed Kolmogorov–Arnold superposition structure (sum of univariate g_q composed with Ψ_q) and the C² smoothness of outer functions fail for general rationally independent λ. The algorithm can produce undefined output. Theorem MainResult's conclusion is unsupported in this regime.
issues.title: Outer-function construction is ill-defined for general rationally independent λ
issues.why_classification: Excluding the advertised 'rationally independent' regime (the generic case, central to Kahane-type Kolmogorov–Arnold representations) is a major loss of scope. No source-supported resolution keeps both regimes; a speculative repair would need new algorithm design and proof.

issues.failure_explanation: Equation (3.7) bounds |f(x) − f(c_q^j)| using the Euclidean distance to the nearest center (≤ √d Nδ/2). But the proof for q ∉ Q applies this bound to the image-closest center from (2.34), which minimizes |Ψ_q(x) − a_q^j|. These metrics can disagree: for d = 2 with Sprecher-like λ₁ ≈ 1/N and λ₂ ≈ 1, a gap deviation in x₂ of order h/2 is compensated by shifting the x₁ index by ≈ N/2 steps, giving a Euclidean distance ≈ 1/2 instead of O(h). The Hölder bound then yields O(1/N) per uncovered level instead of O(h^α/N). The claimed rate O(h^α) holds only when h^α ≳ d/N (i.e. α(1+γ) ≤ 1 for J = N^{1+γ}); for α(1+γ) > 1 the actual rate is O(1/N), not O(N^{−α(1+γ)}).

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use the trivial bound 2‖f‖/N for the at most d uncovered-level terms and restrict the parameter regime to h^α ≥ d/N (equivalently J ≤ (N/d)^{1/α}). This preserves the rate O(N^{−α}) and allows limited rate improvement for α < 1.
issues.overall_effect: The bound ‖f − f_N‖_∞ ≤ C h^α in Theorem MainResult is not established for h^α < d/N. The remark claiming improved rate O(N^{−α(1+γ)}) for arbitrary γ ≥ 0 is wrong when α(1+γ) > 1 (e.g. any γ > 0 for Lipschitz f). The rate O(N^{−α}) (γ = 0) is preserved.

issues.failure_explanation: The equality |f(x)/N − g_q(ψ_q(x))| = |f(x)/N − b_q^j| assumes g_q∘Ψ_q(x) = b_q^j = f(c_q^j)/N. But x ∈ C_q^j does not imply x = c_q^j, so Ψ_q(x) ≠ a_q^j and the S-interpolation gives g_q∘Ψ_q(x) ≠ b_q^j in general. The correct bound requires an additional interpolation error term |b_q^j − g_q∘Ψ_q(x)| ≤ |s_{k+1} − s_k|.

issues.failure_explanation: The supporting estimates claim quadratic approximations of C² functions achieve O(1/M⁴) = O(1/N²) error with M = O(√N) points. Standard interpolation theory gives O(1/M²) = O(1/N) at best for piecewise quadratics of C² functions. With the correct rate, the total error |f − f_N^s| ≈ N · O(1/N) = O(1), which does not converge. Furthermore, the claim that derivative bounds are 'constant above' contradicts earlier estimates showing g_q' grows as N^{(1+γ)(1−α)} for α < 1.
